source_note: Patterns below are condensed from CTAF publications that were downloaded and read. They are documented cases and warning signs. They are not transaction-level training rows. Numeric gates used by the rule engine, when present, are marked operational_gate and are not figures printed by CTAF.

patterns.transaction_behavior: Companies with no declared turnover are funded by transfers from many people, presented as investments in commercial paper, while related share sales are used to simulate activity.
documented_warning_signs: Declared tax turnover is zero while bank flows are large.
No share purchases for the issuing companies over three years.
Repeated share sales to related parties.
Promised yields described as abnormally high versus sector practice.
patterns.operational_gate: Fire only when declared annual revenue is exactly zero and at least five distinct payers fund the receiver within 30 days. CTAF did not publish that payer count.

patterns.transaction_behavior: Cash deposits and cheque proceeds move through one account, with deposits and withdrawals synchronized, and no credible economic justification for the volume.
documented_warning_signs: Volume is inconsistent with the customer's economic profile.
No credible economic justification.
Cash deposits and withdrawals are tightly synchronized.
patterns.operational_gate: The rule uses cash or cheque instruments plus a 6-hour in-and-out ratio. It does not use occupation, age, or nationality. The case amounts are not a threshold.

patterns.transaction_behavior: Accounts opened in Tunisia receive funds from abroad and transfer them onward to foreign beneficiaries, with no apparent link and no real activity in Tunisia.
documented_warning_signs: Account used to receive and immediately redistribute cross-border funds.
No economic justification and no effective activity in Tunisia.
Remote control of the account.
patterns.operational_gate: Requires cross-border inbound funding and a cross-border onward payment within 24 hours covering at least 70 percent of that inflow, from at least two distinct originators. Country of either side alone does not fire the rule.

patterns.transaction_behavior: A small group receives and sends many instant money orders with no economic link, then uses crypto purchases and sales in dinars and electronic foreign-currency payments to reach foreign betting platforms.
documented_warning_signs: Many instant money orders without an economic or personal link.
Betting or crypto payment role is actually indicated.
Foreign-currency electronic payments used to reach betting platforms.
patterns.operational_gate: Requires both a betting or crypto indicator on the payment and at least four money-order counterparties in 30 days. A money order alone, or a country alone, does not fire.

patterns.transaction_behavior: Occasional customers receive several money orders in a short period after senders report fraud. Instruments are instant dinar money orders and international money orders.
documented_warning_signs: Occasional customer.
Several money orders in a short period.
No economic link.
The case also describes social-media account takeover. Age, region, and occupation from the case are not used as rules.
patterns.operational_gate: Requires an explicit occasional-customer flag and at least three inbound money orders in 7 days. The 380-4000 TND band is cited, not used as a detector.

patterns.transaction_behavior: Companies declaring IT services are funded mainly by cash and then transfer dinar balances abroad without the required authorization. The real activity described was passenger transport.
documented_warning_signs: Heavy cash funding.
Declared activity does not match the observed financial activity.
Transfers abroad without the authorization the case says was required.
patterns.operational_gate: Requires a declared IT or software activity together with both cash funding and a cross-border transfer in 30 days. Declared activity alone does not fire.

patterns.transaction_behavior: One occasional customer collects many international money orders, with no economic justification. The 2024 case is 46 orders totaling 76445 TND over four months. A separate bulletin case is 57 Western Union or MoneyGram orders totaling 60943.24 TND over eight months.
documented_warning_signs: Repeated international money orders to one collector.
No economic or contractual justification.
Sender origin is described in the case. Origin, nationality, and ethnicity are not used as rule conditions.
patterns.source_page: CTAF Rapport d'activité 2024, pp. 28-29; CTAF bulletin 2020-2025, p. 16
patterns.operational_gate: At least eight inbound cross-border money orders to the same receiver in 120 days. That gate is below the documented counts of 46 and 57 and is not itself a CTAF statistic.

patterns.transaction_behavior: Bulletin warning signs that can be checked from payment fields: unjustified origin or destination, repeated international transfers, heavy cash use, many international money orders from unrelated people, sudden activity, frequent unexplained FX, large cash followed by immediate withdrawal, a bank account funded by many unrelated originators, and an occasional customer doing frequent or large operations.
documented_warning_signs: Sanctions listing is already handled by the sanctions layer.
Demographic breakdowns in the bulletin (age, gender, nationality, residence) are not encoded as rules.
patterns.operational_gate: Used as the citation for the young-entity and many-unrelated-originator behavior already covered by the 2024 case rules. No extra score is produced from this indicator list alone.
